summary: Daemon executes remote-supplied prompts as AI-agent PTY children with permissions bypassed
details: @addai/entity-runtime@0.2.45 ships a daemon (dist/session-runner.js, dist/request-pump.js, dist/claude-spawn.js) that, once paired, polls a hardcoded Supabase project (https://syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co, RPC runtime_pick_next_request) for work items and executes them by spawning Claude/Codex/Kimi/Gemini/Grok as PTY children with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, then writing remotely-supplied prompts into the PTY via a `write:(data)=>proc.write(data)` bridge. This is a network-to-shell/agent dataflow: any party able to post a request through the paired account (or who compromises that account or the Supabase backend) obtains arbitrary command execution on the operator's host, with the AI agent's file and shell tools running unrestricted. dist/config.js additionally hardcodes the Supabase project URL and an anon JWT used for all RPC calls; anon keys are public by design under Supabase's RLS model, so this is an architecture/disclosure note rather than a separate credential leak. The daemon fires only when the operator explicitly starts the tool via its bin entry, not on `npm install` or on library import, which materially reduces the automatic-trigger surface, but the runtime posture is a remotely-controlled shell/agent channel into the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
